statement: Five quiz scores are whole numbers from 0 to 100, and their mean is 92. What is the lowest that the smallest score could be?

choices.misconception: I thought any score could be 0, forgetting the mean of 92 has to be reached.
I worked as if there were four scores in total: three of 100 and one more, with mean 92.
I thought the lowest score could sit as far below 92 as 100 is above it, giving 92 - 8.
I thought no score could be below the mean.

hints: To make one score small, make the others as big as possible.
Turn the mean into a total. The smallest score is lowest when the other four take the largest values allowed, so bound it by subtracting their greatest possible total.
The five scores total 5 × 92 = 460, and the other four can total at most 400.

solutions.reliable: The five scores total 5 × 92 = 460. The other four scores are each at most 100, so together at most 400, and the smallest score is at least 460 - 400 = 60. The scores 60, 100, 100, 100, 100 show 60 is possible. The transferable idea: to push one value to an extreme, push all the others to the opposite extreme, then check the bound is reached.
solutions.elegant: Each of the four top scores can be at most 8 above the mean, so together they are at most 32 above it. The scores balance around the mean, so the smallest is at most 32 below it: 92 - 32 = 60.

whyOnTest: Bounding settles extreme-value questions quickly: push the other values to their limits, and the traps forget the count or the limit.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
